note: The decisions AWK-23's migration executes, separated from the script that
applies them. Read by merge_composers.py, asserted by merge-composers.test.ts.
Everything here is a DECISION, not a derivation. The 25 contaminated records,
their canonical targets, the arranger surnames and the 24 records to create are
all computed live from cleaned `sortName` -- deliberately, because ADR-0005
establishes that resolving them by id shape silently misses exactly the three
records holding hand-curated dates. What cannot be derived, and so lives here,
is the verb vocabulary, the two arrangement pairs, and the scope guard.
ADR-0005's four verbs, keyed by the marker the source actually writes inside
the composer's name. Flattening these to `Arrangement` would put a factual
error on 12 of the 25 pages: Ravel ORCHESTRATED Pictures, Roven TRANSCRIBED
Kindertotenlieder, and Mauceri EDITED the Psycho selections.
The only two pairs archive-wide where the archive holds BOTH the original and
the arrangement. Data, never detection: `work` is otherwise one entry per
(composer, title) throughout, so a rule matching same-titled works would have
nothing to find here and would false-link the moment a genuine second setting
is added.
Kindertotenlieder's original is PRE-TENURE. The link therefore points at a
work with no route, deliberately -- ADR-0005's landmine. Any UI following it
must tolerate a target that has no page.

pairs.why: Ellington. Both titles are character-identically `The Nutcracker Suite`.
Roven. The original is pre-tenure and has no page.

note: In scope means TENURE, not attendance: `concert.attended` is non-null. Unset
is the 122 pre-tenure seed rows (ADR-0006), `false` is the 6 concerts Alex
missed -- and those 6 are still his history, so their works are in scope.
Reading scope as `attended == true` yields 121/354/326 and only 17 of the 25
contaminated records, silently leaving 8 behind.
These are ABORT thresholds, not documentation. `--force` downgrades them to
warnings. A drift here means the archive moved underneath this migration and
the scope must be re-derived by a human before 25 records are deleted.
The first three are STRICT in both directions -- this migration does not
create or destroy a concert, a program item or a work, so they must read the
same before and after. The two contamination counts have TWO valid states,
and `afterMigration` holds the second: a completed run legitimately reports
0 in scope and 12 archive-wide. Without that, a re-run of a migration that
has already succeeded aborts on its own past work, which is exactly the
false alarm that teaches an operator to reach for --force.
